function.mechanism: Binds fungal/helminth tubulin and disrupts microtubule-dependent cellular processes; used to limit post-harvest fungal spoilage.

adi.basis: EFSA 2022 opinion uses ADI 0.1 mg/kg bw/day (and ARfD 0.1 mg/kg bw) derived in EU pesticide peer review.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA reported no consumer risk for assessed uses in the 2022 confirmatory-data review, but noted endocrine-disruption criteria for thyroid modality and remaining uncertainty for benzimidazole in some animal-commodity contexts; EU legal text states E233 is no longer permitted as a food additive.

fda.cfr_citation: No direct food-additive/GRAS listing found in 21 CFR parts 172/173/180/181/182/184/186; current Title 21 hits are veterinary drug sections 21 CFR 520.2382 and 21 CFR 524.1484g.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database reports ADI range 0-0.1 mg/kg bw for thiabendazole/tiabendazole.

notable_bans: European Union food-additive status: E233 no longer permitted (Commission Directive 2009/10/EC recital).

concerns.summary: EFSA referenced peer-review conclusions that thiabendazole meets endocrine-disruption criteria for humans for thyroid modality.
Zebrafish developmental study reported apoptosis, oxidative stress, altered PI3K/Akt and MAPK pathways, and organ-level toxicity including neurodevelopment-related effects.
A 2025 post-harvest fungicide study including thiabendazole reported mutagenicity and DNA-strand-break findings in Ames/comet assays.
ABCG2 transporter study indicates enhanced secretion of a thiabendazole metabolite into milk in experimental models, relevant to residue exposure pathways.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2022 confirmatory-data review reported no consumer risk identified for assessed uses.
EFSA long-term dietary estimate reported up to 35% of ADI in highest modeled subgroup (NL toddler).

populations: NL toddlers (highest modeled chronic intake in EFSA 2022 remained below ADI)
high consumers of certain produce for acute exposure scenarios
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA did not report chronic ADI exceedance in assessed scenarios; it did report acute-margin concerns including papaya ARfD exceedance in model outputs and narrow margins for some commodities.

risk_assessment.rationale: For E233 as a food additive, EU regulatory withdrawal (no longer permitted) is the dominant factor. Additional concern signals include EFSA endocrine-disruption classification context and recent mechanistic/genotoxic studies, even though ADI-based residue frameworks still indicate controlled scenarios can remain below reference values.
key_factors: EU legal withdrawal of E233 as a food additive
No Title 21 direct food-additive/GRAS listing found in key FDA CFR food-additive parts
EFSA 2022 endocrine-disruption criterion noted for thyroid modality
Recent experimental evidence indicating developmental/mechanistic and genotoxic concerns
JECFA and EFSA still provide ADI-based risk-management frameworks for residue contexts
